title: Life in Weeks Solution
summary: Walks through the Life in Weeks exercise: take an age as a function parameter, assume a lifespan of 90 and fixed unit counts, compute remaining days, weeks and months, and log an exact sentence built by concatenation.

concepts.heading: Exercise logic
points: The function lifeInWeeks(age) receives the current age as its parameter.
Assumptions given by the exercise: 365 days, 52 weeks and 12 months per year, and a lifespan of 90 years.
Compute yearsRemaining = 90 - age first, then multiply by 365, 52 and 12 to get days, weeks and months left.
Build the output sentence by breaking the string at each placeholder and concatenating the numbers with +.
The automated checker compares the text exactly, so spacing, capitalisation, commas and the full stop must match the sample output.

concepts.heading: Verifying
points: Test with a known age: age 12 gives 78 years left, so 28470 days, 4056 weeks and 936 months.
The exercise runs in an online editor with a check-solution button; the code body goes inside the provided function and the call passes an actual age.

task.name: Life in Weeks
task.starting_point: Online coding exercise with an empty lifeInWeeks(age) function.
task.goal: Log exactly: You have X days, Y weeks, and Z months left. for a lifespan of 90.
steps: Compute days, weeks and months by multiplying by 365, 52 and 12.
console.log the sentence, concatenating the three values.
Call lifeInWeeks with a test age and compare the output text exactly.
task.expected_result: lifeInWeeks(12) logs You have 28470 days, 4056 weeks, and 936 months left.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 14 - Introduction to Javascript ES6/14.13 - Life in Weeks Coding Exercise

pitfalls: Typos or wrong punctuation in the sentence fail the exact-match checker.
Reference repo calls lifeInWeeks(18) and subtracts totals instead of computing years first; equivalent maths.
(Extra) Ages over 90 give negative results; not handled.
